Settings and performance

Open Settings with Esc in a world, or from the start menu. Settings are saved inside each world, so a new world copies the settings you have now.

Voxelgame main dd29d91 · 4 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides

Open the settings

  1. In a world, press Esc to pause. Click Settings.
  2. On the start menu, click Settings. Click Back to return.
  3. Move between the General, Audio, World and Debug tabs with the mouse or Tab and Shift + Tab.
Key or actionWhat it does
Up / Down arrowsSelect a row.
Left / Right arrows, or EnterChange the selected value.
Click a chip or drag a sliderSet a value directly.
Right-click a rowStep that value back. This is not shown in the game.

Hover a row label for a short description. The world stops advancing while Settings is open. Settings menu basics

General tab

  • Shader: None, Fast (default) or Cinematic. None is plain lighting for weak graphics cards. Fast adds sun shadows, sun rays and haze. Cinematic refines the shadows and rays and adds reflective water, at a higher frame-time cost. Shader quality: None, Fast, Cinematic
  • Horizon distance: 8, 16, 32, 48, 64 (default), 96, 128, 192, 256 or 512 chunks. A chunk is 16 m, so 64 chunks reach about 1 km and 512 chunks reach about 8 km. Blocks close to you stay at full detail either way. Horizon distance
  • Frame limit: 60 (default), 120, 240 or Unlimited. The game does not use vsync, so this limit sets the pace. Study Grove always runs at about 30 FPS. Frame limit
  • Atmospheric fog: Light, Balanced (default) or Dense. Dense hides far terrain. The haze gets stronger with a longer horizon. Weather fog is separate. Atmospheric fog (haze) presets
  • Field of view: 60 to 96 degrees, in steps of 2 (default 72). A wider view shows more without changing how fast you move. Field of view
  • GUI size: Auto (default), Small, Normal or Large. Auto uses 1.25x up to 1280x720 and 1.5x from 1920x1080 up. Small is 1.0x, Normal 1.25x and Large 1.75x. A small window caps the size so the UI still fits at least 800x450. GUI size
  • Chunk fade-in: on by default. New terrain fades in over 0.6 seconds. Turn it off to make terrain appear at once. Terrain prepared on the loading screen is always fully visible. Chunk fade-in

Audio tab

  • Master volume: 0% (mute) to 100% (default). It sets music, sound effects and nature sounds together, and applies at once. There is no separate volume for effects or ambience. Master volume
  • Music: turn the music on or off. Sound effects keep playing either way.
  • Music speed: 0.5x to 2.0x in steps of 0.1x. Tempo and pitch change together.
  • Previous and Next choose a song. The playlist then moves on by itself and loops. If no songs are found, the tab says so. Music: on/off, speed and song choice

Wind, rain, storms, forest, caves, birds, night wildlife, ponds and streams fade in and out around you without a setting. The ambience goes quiet in menus and underwater. Nature ambience

Debug tab and overlays

Most of the Debug tab is for checking the game, but two rows are useful for play. The FPS and coordinates box shows your frame rate with its limit, your X, Y and Z in metres and your biome. It is on by default, and it is back on after every load. FPS and coordinates readout

Key or actionWhat it does
F3Show or hide the performance overlay. It shows the frame time against your frame budget, the worst recent frame and the CPU work for the last half second.
F7Show or hide chunk borders. The chunk you stand in is gold.
F8Cycle the LOD view: Off, Tint and Colors. Cyan is full detail, and the other colours mark the distant stages.
F9Turn all three diagnostics off, or all on in Tint.
Tip. F7, F8 and F9 are reset to off when a world loads. F3 resets too. The Debug tab has the same switches. Chunk borders (F7), LOD view (F8) and all diagnostics (F9) Performance overlay (F3)
  • Voxel view: Off (default), Edges, which tints every block border, or X-ray, which draws only the outlines. Voxel view: block edges and X-ray outlines
  • Distant terrain: on by default. It draws the low-detail horizon beyond the nearby chunks. Turning it off saves work on slow machines. The view then ends at the loaded terrain, and new chunks can appear at that edge when you travel fast. Distant terrain on/off

If the game runs slowly

  1. Set Shader to None.
  2. Lower Horizon distance to 32 or 16 chunks.
  3. Turn Distant terrain off on the Debug tab. The view then ends at the loaded terrain.
  4. Press F3 to see whether the frame time is above your frame budget. Red marks work that uses more than one CPU core or over half the frame budget.

Large horizons cost the most. One offscreen test on an Intel Iris Xe measured about 1.8 to 1.9 GiB of distant-terrain vertex buffers and about 37 to 39 ms of world GPU work at 256 to 512 chunks. Your numbers will differ. The overlay does not show GPU timing in normal play.

Settings and your worlds

Graphics, audio and GUI settings are saved inside each world file. Create world copies the settings you have now. Loading another world switches to that world's own settings. Settings are stored inside each world

Not in the game yet

Planned, not in the game. Planned: a 1024-chunk horizon. The largest option today is 512 chunks.
Planned, not in the game. Planned: live GPU timings in the F3 overlay. Today the GPU box says it is unavailable in normal play.
Planned, not in the game. Not in the game: the game does not keep the screen awake. Your system's power settings apply, including during long Study Grove sessions.
Planned, not in the game. Planned: album art beside the song title, and a credits-only piece of music.

How this guide was checked

Each row, its default and its range come from the game source at the audited commit, b261ea8. The performance advice follows the notes on each row, including one offscreen GPU test on an Intel Iris Xe.

Voxelgame main dd29d91, committed 10 October 2026; guide written 12 October 2026. Source-checked, not play-tested, and no screenshots exist yet. The GPU numbers are from one test machine and will differ on yours. Features covered, with their source evidence: Settings menu basics, Shader quality: None, Fast, Cinematic, Horizon distance, Frame limit, Atmospheric fog (haze) presets, Field of view, GUI size, Chunk fade-in, FPS and coordinates readout, Voxel view: block edges and X-ray outlines, Distant terrain on/off, Performance overlay (F3), Chunk borders (F7), LOD view (F8) and all diagnostics (F9), Master volume, Music: on/off, speed and song choice, Nature ambience, Settings are stored inside each world.
